name: Mike Collins
incumbencyStatus: challenger — currently U.S. Representative, Georgia 10th District (2023–present)

priorRoles: Co-founder and owner, trucking company (early 1990s–present; grew from 1 semi-truck to 115-truck fleet employing 100+ Georgians)
Chairman of the Board, Associated Credit Union (one of Georgia's largest)
President, Butts County Chamber of Commerce
biography.education: B.A. Business Administration, Georgia State University, 1990
biography.background: Small business owner and entrepreneur. Son of former U.S. Rep. Mac Collins (GA-8, 1993–2005). Born July 2, 1967, Jackson, Georgia. Strong MAGA alignment; known for aggressive social media presence. Won GA-10 seat in 2022 after Jody Hice declined to seek reelection; won runoff over Vernon Jones. Re-elected 2024 (64.5% to 35.5%). Announced Senate candidacy July 28, 2025.
biography.family: Married to Leigh Ann Collins; three children (Dakota, Dylan, Summer); six grandchildren

campaignWebsite.notes: WebFetch was unavailable; content reconstructed from search snippets referencing the live site

statedPositions.quote: It's time to send a trucker to the U.S. Senate to steamroll the radical left, deliver on President Trump's America First agenda, and put the people of Georgia back in the driver's seat.
statedPositions.notes: Launch video quote, confirmed across multiple outlets

statedPositions.quote: I'm unapologetically pro God, pro Trump, pro Second Amendment. I am for a strong military peace through strength works. I am 100% America first through and through. If it's not good for Georgia and if it's not good for our country, then count me out.
statedPositions.notes: Campaign rally in Jackson, GA; crowd of 400+

statedPositions.quote: Mike started his first trucking business at age 25, starting out with one semi-truck and growing to employ over one hundred drivers today. Mike has led three successful businesses that have grown Georgia's economy.

We should finish the wall, bring back remain in Mexico, and stop letting anyone who says they're seeking asylum into our country. If the Senate would take up H.R. 2 passed nearly a year ago, we could fix this problem.
statedPositions.notes: AJC/ACC Voter Guide 2024 congressional questionnaire direct quote

statedPositions.quote: The federal government needs to stop pushing these ridiculous 'Green Energy' policies on America.
statedPositions.notes: AJC/ACC Voter Guide 2024, response to climate change question

statedPositions.quote: Drill here, drill now. Bidenflation continues to hurt our economy and hard working Americans. We've passed bills in the House to bring our country back to energy independence, secure our border, and invest in America.
statedPositions.notes: AJC/ACC Voter Guide 2024, response to cost of living question
iVoterGuide scale: C = keep Medicaid and Medicare but no other taxpayer-funded programs; D = abolish all taxpayer-funded healthcare. Response from 2022 but no 2024 survey completed.

statedPositions.quote: Abortion providers, including Planned Parenthood, should not receive funds from federal, state, or local governments (including Title X grants).
statedPositions.notes: iVoterGuide 2022 survey; consistent with 2025 personhood bill cosponsor action
iVoterGuide 2022 survey; consistent with GGO 100% survey and NRA ~92% rating

statedPositions.quote: We need to stop all illegal immigration and consider a moratorium on immigration until we can reform the immigration laws. We need to look at reducing the legal immigration as well.
statedPositions.notes: iVoterGuide 2022; strong position on reducing both illegal AND legal immigration

statedPositions.quote: Americans are already seeing the effects of inflation and a stagnant economy, and something must be done. In Congress, I will work to enact a balanced budget amendment, cut federal spending, reduce the national debt and limit the size and scope of government.
statedPositions.notes: VoteSmart; consistent with House votes opposing fiscal legislation he deemed too expensive

statedPositions.quote: You can set it up to increase your revenue, and you can do that by lowering taxes and making it more advantageous for people to work, and to get off of Medicaid, get off of Social Security, get back in the workforce.
statedPositions.notes: Said on XTRA 106.3 right-wing talk radio, June 5 2025, defending reconciliation bill. Generated significant backlash.

statedPositions.quote: Abolish the ATF. Repeal the NFA. Support national constitutional carry.
statedPositions.notes: Signed Georgia Gun Owners 100% pro-gun survey Dec 9, 2025. Cosponsored bill to abolish ATF and repeal NFA.

statedPositions.quote: The problem is not the gun.

statedPositions.quote: With President Trump in the White House and me in the U.S. Senate, the hardworking men and women of this country will not be forgotten anymore.

keyVotes.notes: Voted against debt ceiling deal; one of 71 Republicans to oppose final passage. Position: opposed as insufficiently conservative, wanted deeper cuts.

keyVotes.bill: TRANQ Act (Testing, Rapid Analysis, and Narcotic Quality Act)
keyVotes.notes: Introduced by Collins; passed both House and Senate, signed into law Dec 2023. Bipartisan fentanyl/xylazine drug testing legislation.

Collins' signature legislation. Requires ICE to detain undocumented immigrants charged with theft. Passed House in 118th Congress; passed both chambers Jan 2025 and signed by Trump. Named for murdered Georgia nursing student.

keyVotes.bill: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1, 119th Congress — reconciliation)
keyVotes.notes: House passed 215-214 (May 2025), then final 218-214 (July 3 2025). Collins publicly defended bill. Bill includes $800B Medicaid cuts, ACA subsidy reductions, tax cuts. CBO: 11.8 million people would lose health coverage by 2034. Collins called for people to 'get off Medicaid' in defense of the bill.

keyVotes.bill: Personhood bill — life beginning at conception (Eric Burlison bill)
keyVotes.notes: Cosponsored legislation recognizing personhood starting at conception, Jan 2025. Consistent with prior iVoterGuide positions opposing Planned Parenthood funding.

controversies.description: In November 2025, the House Ethics Committee announced an investigation into Collins and his chief of staff Brandon Phillips. The Office of Congressional Conduct had transmitted the matter on Oct 7, 2025. Allegation: Collins used government funds to benefit his chief of staff, who allegedly hired his girlfriend to work for Collins' office.
controversies.collinsResponse: Called it 'nothing but a desperate and baseless attack'; said they 'look forward to the Ethics Committee completing its work and this frivolous complaint being dismissed.'

controversies.description: In November 2025, the Collins campaign released an AI-generated video depicting Sen. Jon Ossoff defending his vote on the 2025 federal government shutdown. The video was fabricated.
controversies.notes: Campaign also released a separate AI-generated video featuring Collins as a shirtless jeans model, referencing an American Eagle/Sydney Sweeney ad.

controversies.description: In March 2024, Collins replied approvingly to an X post from an account ('Garbage Human') with a history of racist and antisemitic content, implicitly disparaging a Washington Post journalist for being Jewish. Collins refused to delete the post, drawing bipartisan rebukes.

positionConflicts.conflict: Campaign emphasizes fighting for 'hardworking men and women' and Georgians, but June 2025 radio statement explicitly told retirees to 'get off Social Security, get back in the workforce.' Republicans Study Committee (which includes Collins) also proposed a budget cutting Social Security.

Georgia Democratic Party analysis: Collins voted for One Big Beautiful Bill which would raise health care premiums an average 345% for GA-10 constituents, and strip coverage from up to 750,000 Georgians. Collins describes himself as pro-business and pro-worker.
positionConflicts.notes: Partisan source; CBO independently projects 11.8M national coverage losses from the bill.

positionConflicts.conflict: Voted AGAINST Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (too liberal on spending for him), yet voted FOR One Big Beautiful Bill that adds trillions to deficit according to CRFB. Heritage Action 98% score suggests ideological purity, but OBBBA does not fit traditional deficit-hawk conservatism.

billsSponsored.note: GovTrack 2024 report shows Collins sponsored bills primarily in: Environmental Protection (28%), Science/Technology/Communications (22%), Crime and Law Enforcement (22%), Immigration (17%), Taxation (11%). Introduced fewer bills than typical Georgia delegation members.

evidenceSummary.notes: Two-year House record (2023–2025) provides moderate evidence base. Heritage Action 98% and LCV 1% are the two most reliable composite signals — they paint a consistent picture of a hard-right legislator with near-zero environmental interest and near-total conservative economic alignment. Primary gaps: housing/zoning (no record), criminal justice (limited record). The Social Security radio statement (June 2025) is a particularly significant piece of evidence — it goes beyond standard Republican fiscal rhetoric into explicit advocacy for safety net reduction.
